pebbles.title: FloodNet ultrasonic depth sensors (NYC)

narration.short: FloodNet sensors and historical flood events near this address.

provenance.source_name: FloodNet (New York University and The City University of New York)
provenance.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
provenance.citation: FloodNet street flood sensors. Flood events and sensor status read from the FloodNet Data API (api.floodnet.nyc, an early-access beta) at the retrieval time shown. A flood event is a series of depth measurements greater than 10 mm at the sensor (FloodNet's definition); a depth is measured at one point and does not show the depth on every part of the street. Riprap counts the events the API marks as verified by a person. FloodNet's published cautions about a depth: "most FloodNet sensors are mounted over sidewalks and are thus unable to measure floods in the roadbed until the water rises above the height of the curb"; the depth at the street's lowest point differs from the reading by the sensor's height above that point; "a single anomalous data point, measured during a flood event" may exaggerate a maximum depth; and a sensor may miss a flood "if it was offline and awaiting repair or had not been deployed yet or retired" (FloodNet's NYC Open Data description, dataset aq7i-eu5q). Ten rows of FloodNet's deployments table are NOAA and USGS tide gauges (deploy_type "tidal"); Riprap does not count them as FloodNet sensors. Riprap names no sensor, because FloodNet's licence forbids reposting its records: each verified event can be found by its date and depth in FloodNet's own table on NYC Open Data, "FloodNet: Street Flooding Events Measured by FloodNet Sensors" (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/aq7i-eu5q), and on its dashboard (https://dataviz.floodnet.nyc).
